# Page 1^page=1
5 Best Claude Code MCPs You Need to Install 👾 These five turn Claude Code from a chatbot into a weapon. Install commands for each below or paste the one master prompt at the bottom that installs all five in a single message. --- 1. Playwright MCP What it does: Claude controls a real browser. Clicks buttons, fills forms, pulls data off any page. Install command: claude mcp add playwright -- npx @playwright/mcp@latest When to use it: - You need to scrape a site that has no API - You want Claude to test your own product UI - You're automating a repeatable web task (lead gen, form filling, status checks) --- 2. Context7 What it does: Pulls live documentation into the chat. Claude stops hallucinating outdated APIs. Install command: claude mcp add --scope user context7 -- npx -y @upstash/context7-mcp When to use it: - You're using a library that updated in the last 6 months - Claude keeps writing code that doesn't match current syntax - You want version-specific docs (React 18 vs 19, Next 14 vs 16) --- 3. Sequential Thinking What it does: Built by Anthropic. Claude stops guessing. It plans the whole problem step by step, branches when it's wrong, and revises before touching code. Plan mode times ten.

# Page 2^page=2
Install command: claude mcp add sequential-thinking -- npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-sequential-thinking When to use it: - You're tackling a multi-step problem with unclear scope - You want Claude to think before it codes - You're tired of one-shot answers that miss the bigger picture --- 4. Codex Plugin What it does: Deploy OpenAI's Codex (GPT-5.4) inside Claude Code. Codex actively challenges Claude's code. Two models, two companies, one session. Output gets insanely better. Install command: /plugin marketplace add openai/codex-plugin-cc /plugin install codex@codex-plugin-cc [CONFIRM: exact slash command syntax per github.com/openai/codex-plugin-cc README] When to use it: - You want a second opinion before shipping anything important - You're stuck on a bug Claude can't see - Run /codex:review for a read-only second look, /codex:adversarial-review to have it challenge Claude's design, or /codex:rescue to hand the whole task off --- 5. Knowledge Graph Memory MCP What it does: Also from Anthropic. Gives Claude a brain that persists. Stores three things in a local file all about you: entities, relationships, and observations. Survives across sessions. Install command: claude mcp add --scope project memory -e MEMORY_FILE_PATH=./.claude/memory.json -- npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-memory When to use it: - You're tired of re-explaining your business every new chat - You want Claude to reference decisions you made weeks ago - You sync the JSONL file across machines and Claude remembers you everywhere ---

# Page 3^page=3
INSTALL ALL FIVE — Master Prompt Paste this entire block into a fresh Claude Code session. It will run each install in order, confirm each one, and show you the final list. Install these 5 MCP servers and plugins for me, one at a time. After each command, confirm it ran successfully before moving to the next. If any command fails, stop and tell me the exact error. 1. claude mcp add playwright -- npx @playwright/mcp@latest 2. claude mcp add --scope user context7 -- npx -y @upstash/context7-mcp 3. claude mcp add sequential-thinking -- npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-sequential-thinking 4. /plugin marketplace add openai/codex-plugin-cc /plugin install codex@codex-plugin-cc 5. claude mcp add --scope project memory -e MEMORY_FILE_PATH=./.claude/memory.json -- npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-memory After all five are installed, run /mcp to list every connected server and confirm everything shows as connected. If anything is missing or red, tell me which one and walk me through fixing it. --- FOLLOW FOR MORE
